title: Aviation Laws Amendment (Australian Ownership and Operation) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish Australian ownership and operating criteria for airlines seeking access to domestic routes, covering equity ownership, aircraft maintenance and crew domicile.
An airline would need 51 per cent ownership by Australian citizens or residents, at least 80 per cent of aircraft maintenance performed in Australia and crews domiciled here.
Companies with access to Australian routes would bear the onus of showing that they satisfy the proposed definition, including its ownership and operational criteria.
changes: The ownership test would recognise holdings by Australian citizens or residents, including share ownership.
The maintenance criterion would require at least 80 per cent of an airline’s aircraft maintenance to occur domestically.
The crew criterion would require airline crews to be domiciled in Australia.
summary.affected: Airlines accessing Australian domestic routes, their Australian citizen or resident owners and their crews are affected.
